about: Bug Hoops practice (the Shootaround): open at any mastery. Click the line with the bug to shoot. These are practice problems, never the transfer scenarios, so the real transfer check stays fresh. Python items carry a `check` that fails as written and a `fix` for the answer line that makes it pass; tests/test_gym_games.py runs both.

items.title: The club door
items.story: Anyone 16 or over may enter, and younger visitors may enter with an adult.
items.check: assert can_enter(16, False) and can_enter(10, True) and not can_enter(10, False)
items.why: The test is backwards: it lets in young visitors who have no adult. It should be if with_adult:.

items.title: Free shipping
items.story: Members always ship free; everyone else needs an order of 50 or more.
items.check: assert free_shipping(50, False) and free_shipping(10, True) and not free_shipping(49, False)
items.why: An order of exactly 50 should ship free, but total > 50 says no. "50 or more" is >= 50.

items.title: Adding up to n
items.story: Return 1 + 2 + ... + n.
items.why: i < n stops before n is added, so sum_to(3) gives 3, not 6. The loop must run while i <= n.

items.title: The first cold day
items.story: Return the first negative temperature in the list, or None if there is none.
items.check: assert first_negative([3, -1, -5]) == -1 and first_negative([1, 2]) is None
items.why: The loop keeps going after the first negative and overwrites result, so it returns the last one. Return t (or break) as soon as it is found.

items.title: The last few songs
items.story: Return the last n songs of a playlist.
items.why: The last n items start at len(songs) - n. The extra - 1 starts one early and returns n + 1 songs.

items.title: Every other seat
items.story: Return the seats at positions 0, 2, 4 and so on.
items.why: range(1, ...) starts at the second seat, so it picks positions 1, 3, 5. Start at 0.

items.title: The till
items.story: Return the total of all the prices.
items.why: return total is inside the loop, so the function returns after the first price. Move it out of the loop.

items.title: Make it loud
items.story: shout("hi") should give "HI!".
items.why: loud + "!" builds a new string and throws it away. Strings never change in place: keep the result with loud = loud + "!".

items.title: The visitor counter
items.story: Each call adds one to the global visits and returns it.
items.why: Assigning to visits inside the function makes it local, so visits + 1 reads a local with no value yet: UnboundLocalError. Declare global visits first.

items.title: A fresh scorecard
items.story: With no list given, start a new list holding just this score.
items.fix:
def add_score(score, scores=None):
    scores = [] if scores is None else scores
items.why: The default list is built once, when def runs, and every call shares it, so scores pile up between calls. Default to None and make a new list inside.

items.title: Hours to minutes
items.story: The hours come in as text, like " 2 ". Return the minutes, 120.
items.why: hours is still a str, and "2" * 60 repeats the text 60 times. Convert it: int(hours_text.strip()).

items.title: Shelf labels
items.story: label(3) should give "Item 3".
items.why: n is an int, and str + int raises TypeError. Convert it with str(n) or use an f-string.

items.title: The mystery resistor
items.story: A 12 V supply drives 4 mA through a resistor. Find its resistance.

items.title: Volts across the coil
items.story: A 2.2 kΩ resistor carries 5 mA. Find the voltage across it.
lines: In base units: R = 2200 Ω, I = 0.005 A
items.why: Ohm's law multiplies: V = 0.005 × 2200 = 11 V.

items.title: Two in a row
items.story: 9 V across 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ in series. Find the current.
lines: The same current flows through both
items.why: Use the total resistance: I = 9 / 3000 = 3 mA.

items.title: The bigger share
items.story: 12 V across 2 kΩ and 4 kΩ in series. Find the voltage across the 4 kΩ.
lines: V across 4 kΩ = 2 mA × 2 kΩ = 4 V
The two drops add up to 12 V
items.why: It used the wrong resistor. V = 2 mA × 4 kΩ = 8 V, and 4 V + 8 V = 12 V.

items.title: Two branches
items.story: 6 V across 2 kΩ and 3 kΩ in parallel. Find the total current.
lines: Each branch has the full 6 V
items.why: Branch currents add: 3 mA + 2 mA = 5 mA.

items.title: Twin heaters
items.story: Two 6 kΩ resistors in parallel. Find their combined resistance.
lines: The result is smaller than either branch
items.why: Adding is the series rule. From 1/R = 2/6, R = 3 kΩ: two equal branches halve the resistance.

items.title: The dead string
items.story: A 9 V series loop of R1, R2 and R3 has stopped working: R2 is open.
lines: An open breaks the only path
V across R1 = I × R1 = 0 V
V across R2 = 0 V, like the others
items.why: With no current the good parts drop nothing, so the full 9 V appears across the open R2.

items.title: Hunting the break
items.story: A 6 V series loop of R1 and R2 is dead. You measure across each part.
lines: So R1 is the open part
items.why: The open part is the one that reads the full supply. R2 reads 6 V, so R2 is open, not R1.

items.title: A bridged resistor
items.story: Three 1 kΩ resistors in series on 9 V, and R3 is shorted.
lines: V across R3 = 4.5 mA × 1 kΩ = 4.5 V
items.why: A shorted part has 0 Ω, so it drops 0 V. The 9 V is shared by R1 and R2.

items.title: More current, not less
items.story: Two 2 kΩ resistors in series on 8 V, and one is shorted.
lines: The short takes one resistor out
So the current falls to 1 mA
items.why: Less resistance means more current: I = 8 / 2000 = 4 mA, up from 2 mA.

items.title: Check the label
items.story: A resistor labelled 1 kΩ reads 3 V with 1.5 mA through it.
lines: So it matches the 1 kΩ label
items.why: 2000 Ω is 2 kΩ, double the label, so it is the wrong part.

items.title: Within tolerance
items.story: A resistor labelled 470 Ω has 9 V across it and 19 mA through it.
lines: That is far below the label
items.why: 19 mA is 0.019 A, so R = 9 / 0.019 ≈ 474 Ω, close to the 470 Ω label: the part is fine.
